often lead to the centralization of political and economic power as governments seek to
maintain control and ensure stability. This centralization can manifest in increased
surveillance, the consolidation of authority in executive branches, and the prioritization
of national security over civil liberties and democratic processes. Such shifts can
undermine state development by diverting resources away from social and economic programs,
fostering inequality, and stifling political dissent. Consequently, the implications for
international development are significant, as centralized power can inhibit collaboration,
reduce foreign investment, and limit the effectiveness of international aid, ultimately
perpetuating cycles of instability and underdevelopment.
